title: Photos Show Today’s Native Americans

image.attribution: LeRoy N. Sanchez, Los Alamos National Laboratory / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Matika Wilbur has a goal that will take her across the United States. She plans to photograph every Native American tribe in the country.

She hopes that her photographs will help end the many stereotypes Americans and others worldwide have of native people.

“When you see us represented in mass media, you see Pocahontas, Dances with Wolves and Twilight,” Ms. Wilbur said. “What you won’t see is doctors and lawyers and …people living in the present.”

Ms. Wilbur herself is a Native American woman of the Swinomish and Tulalip tribes.

She has already been on the road for more than three years.

Ms. Wilbur is a high school teacher as well as a photographer.

“There’s something in this collective consciousness that still believes that Indians are lesser human beings, savage, that we’re conquered,” Ms.Wilbur said. She said false ideas of Native Americans make them feel bad about themselves.

Native American youth have the highest suicide levels in the country. Ms.Wilbur said she hopes her photographs of diverse people will not only inform, but also uplift.

“Hopefully we can create something beautiful and positive, …” she said.
